Milling Gutters, Saws. Gear Gutting Tools and Broaches Sectional Gommiitee. PE 11 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
iinalized by the Milling Gutters, Saws, Gear Cutting Tools and Broaches Sectional Committee, had been 
approved by the Production Engineering Division Council. 

This standard was first published in 1971. Following changes have been made in this revision: 

a) Type A, B, and G slot drills with tanged end and Type E with tapped end specified in earlier 
version are not in much use in the industries, hence deleted. 

b) This version includes: 

i) tolerance on length 
ii) sampling clause. 

c) Title changed from 'Slot milling cutter' to 'Slot drills'. 

IS 6352 : 1991, 'Slot drills with parallel shank — Specification {first revision )' is another standard in this 
series. In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from ISO 1641/2 : 
1978 'End mills and slot drills : Part 2 Milling cutters with morse taper shank', issued by International 
Organization for Standardization ( ISO ). 



IS 6388: 1991 



Indian Standard 

SLOT DRILLS WITH MORSE TAPER SHANKS 

SPECIFICATION 

( First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

This Indian Standard covers dimensions and 
other requirements for slot drills with morse 
taper and tapped end shanks. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

IS Mo. Title 

1715 : 1986 Dimensions for self-holding taper 

( second revision ) 

1830 : 1982 Technical supply conditions for 
milling cutters ( second revision ) 

7778 : 1975 Method for sampling small tools 

3 TYPES 

Slot drills with morse taper shanks shall be of 
following types: 

Type D — Flat face, helical fluted with tapped 

end morse taper shank 
Type F — Concave face, helical fluted with 

tapped end morse taper shank 

4 TERMINOLOGY 

Shall be as given in IS 1830 : 1982 . 

5 DIMENSIONS 

Shall be as given in Table 1. 

6 TOLERANCES 

On '/' and 'Z-i' lengths.

7 MATERIAL AND HARDNESS 

Shall be according to IS 1830 : 1982. 

8 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

8.1 Unless otherwise specified, Type D slot 
drills of short series with right hand helical flutes 
for right hand cutting shall be supplied. 

8.2 The requirements, not covered in this, 
standard, shall conform to the requirements given 
in IS 1830 : 1982. 

8.3 Dimensions for morse taper shanks having 
tapped hole shall be according to IS 1715 : 1986. 

9 SAMPLING 

The sampling and criteria of acceptance shall be 
in accordance with IS 7778 : 1975. 

10 DESIGNATION 

A slot drill with tapped end morse taper shank: 
flat face and helical fluted of Type D having, 
diameter D = 10 mm of short series ( U ) for 
right hand cutting made from high speed steel, 
shall be designated as: 

Slot Drill with Morse Taper Shank IS 6388- 
DIOU 

11 MARKING 

Shall be according to IS 1830 : 1982. 

12 PROTECTIVE COATING AND 
PACKAGING 

Shall be according to IS 1830 : 1982.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 
Acty 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products 
covered by an Indian Standard conveys the jassurance that they have been produced to comply 
with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and 
quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard 
marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a 
further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark 
may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards ^t, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of poodi 
and -attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of ail its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if any, arc 
issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the 
latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving the 
following reference: 

Doc:No, PE 11 (5007)
